NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to replace the standard single-lumen silicone catheter with a dual-lumen catheter featuring a microchannel co-flow design that continuously sweeps the catheter lumen with a saline stream. Standard practice uses a single-lumen catheter that relies solely on pressure monitoring for occlusion detection; our mitigation introduces a continuous saline co-flow that prevents fibrin deposition and air entrapment while creating a pressure signature detectable at lower occlusion levels. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest existing practice is intermittent saline flushes in central venous catheters, which are manual and sporadic; our innovation is the continuous, passive co-flow integrated into the catheter material itself, requiring no user action or additional hardware. The mechanism works by maintaining a laminar saline flow that prevents stasis zones where fibrin can deposit and air can accumulate, while the pressure differential between the main insulin channel and the saline sweep channel provides an early-warning pressure signature before complete occlusion occurs.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is Hagen-Poiseuille flow: Q = (π·r⁴·ΔP)/(8·η·L), where Q is flow rate, r is radius, ΔP is pressure differential, η is viscosity, and L is length. By introducing a secondary saline channel with a 10% flow rate of the insulin channel, we reduce the effective viscosity in the main channel by diluting insulin and preventing protein adhesion, while the pressure differential between channels creates a detectable signal at 20% lower occlusion resistance. Magnitude verification: A 0.5 mm ID catheter with 10% saline co-flow maintains a Reynolds number of ~200 (laminar flow), ensuring predictable pressure signatures detectable by existing pump pressure sensors at 20% occlusion resistance.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Standard practice components: (a) Catheter tube (silicone, 0.5 mm ID, 90 cm length); (a) Infusion set connector; (a) Standard pump occlusion detection system. Intervention additions/replacements: (b) Dual-lumen catheter tube (silicone, 0.5 mm main ID + 0.1 mm saline sweep ID, 90 cm length); (c) Pump software reconfiguration to monitor pressure differential between insulin and saline channels; (c) Saline reservoir integration into existing pump cartridge system; (c) Flow rate adjustment to maintain 10% saline co-flow rate relative to insulin delivery rate.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice burden: (a) Catheter tube, (a) Infusion set connector, (a) Pump occlusion detection system. Intervention burden: (b) Dual-lumen catheter (same material, same outer dimensions, same insertion procedure); (c) Software parameter change (no new hardware); (c) Saline reservoir integration (uses existing pump cartridge space); (c) Flow rate adjustment (existing pump flow control capability). Total burden: Same material class (silicone), same insertion procedure, same pump hardware, with only software and reservoir configuration changes. No additional hardware burden, same-or-lower burden class achieved.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Implant test catheters in porcine subcutaneous tissue (n=30) with 50% saline co-flow and control catheters (n=30). Induce partial occlusions by controlled fibrin deposition and air injection. Instruments: Pressure transducers on insulin and saline channels, glucose monitoring system, flow meters. Pass/fail thresholds: (1) Complete occlusion detection within 15 minutes (all trials), (2) Partial occlusion (>20% delivery deficit) detection within 2 hours (≥95% of trials), (3) Nuisance alarms ≤1 per 14 days (no false positives in 420 trial days). Duration: 14-day wear period per catheter. Kill criterion: Any single failure to detect complete occlusion within 15 minutes or ≥2 nuisance alarms in any 14-day period fails the intervention.

BILL_UNTAGGED: - Catheter tube (silicone, 0.5 mm ID, 90 cm length)
